summary: sc-announcer resolves its sole dependency from an off-registry HTTPS tarball
details: sc-announcer@99.9.1 ships an empty stub (`module.exports = {}`) and declares a single dependency `ltidisafe` sourced from an off-registry HTTPS tarball URL (`https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-4.0.2.tgz`) in package.json rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches that tarball and installs whatever bytes it returns, with no version pin, no integrity hash, and no registry provenance; any lifecycle scripts contained inside the fetched tarball execute on the installer's machine. The implausibly high version number (99.9.1) and dependency-confusion-shaped setup — stub package whose only effect is to pull a URL-sourced dependency — are consistent with a resolution-hijack lure targeting an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
